meetings.label: November 17, 2025
items: External auditor presented the annual audit and federal single audit with no findings to report
School Improvement Plans presented by all five principals and approved
2024–2025 state designations shared: four schools Commendable, one Targeted
Tentative 2025 tax levy presented at 3.37% over the prior extension
Joint Board Safety Notification Protocol and Tiered Case Management approved

Audit: Jeff Rollefson, CPA of Evans, Marshall & Pease, P.C. presented the financial statements and the federal single audit
The financial report was consistent with prior years, and the district complied with federal requirements with no findings to report
School Improvement Plans: SIPs aligned to Strategic Plan priorities: academic growth, equitable access to rigorous curriculum, recruitment and retention, welcoming and safe culture, resource allocation, and community partnerships
Oak Crest: 63% of students to meet growth targets in ELA and 66% in math; reduce Tier II and Tier III intervention counts
Howe: 56% of students to meet or exceed i-Ready growth targets in reading and math; daily morning meetings and Second Step lessons in all classrooms by May 2026
Kenneth Murphy: all K–5 teachers implementing the ELA curriculum with 90% fidelity by May 2026; 30% reduction in behavioral referrals
Newport: students meeting or exceeding i-Ready growth goals; improve climate and culture through family engagement events
BPMS: growth and grade-level targets on i-Ready, plus a 10% decrease in office-managed log entries
2024–2025 Designations: Newport, BPMS, Kenneth Murphy and Oak Crest each designated Commendable; Howe designated Targeted for one subgroup of just over 20 students
Newport increased its overall index score by 13.43, from 52.01 to 65.44
BPMS earned Commendable for a second consecutive year
Kenneth Murphy moved into Commendable status, with ELA scores up 13 points
Oak Crest English Learner proficiency growth on IAR rose from 60.23 to 70.61
Tentative Levy: Frank Adams presented the tentative 2025 levy for review
Extension limited by PTELL to the lesser of 5.0% or CPI, plus new property; the applicable 2025 CPI is 2.9%
Administration proposed a levy request 3.37% over the prior year's extension, intentionally overestimated to capture revenue from new construction
Cost pressures cited: pending union contract renegotiations, health insurance increases of 15% to 35%, purchased services, building maintenance, and special education
Action Items: Donation in excess of $500 approved
School Improvement Plans approved
Joint Board Safety Notification Protocol / Tiered Case Management approved
Board approved supporting the IASB resolution on school bus safety funding and all ten proposed constitutional amendments
Also Noted: Positive Descriptive Praise, Staff Spotlight and the first District Champion Award recipients honored in person
November recognized as School Board Member Appreciation Month
Thanksgiving break November 26–29

meetings.label: May 11, 2026
items: Fall-to-winter i-Ready data presented: districtwide gains in ELA and math grade-level proficiency

i-Ready / SIP Data: Director of Teaching and Learning Traci Griffiths presented fall-to-winter i-Ready assessment data
Against a district goal of 53% of students meeting projected growth targets in ELA and math, overall growth was near or at target across most schools and grade levels
Districtwide, students at or above grade level increased in both ELA and math, while students one or more grade levels below expectations decreased
First-year curriculum implementation challenges were discussed, supported by professional development and instructional coaching
Celebrations included growth in mathematics and progress among kindergarten students; next steps include reviewing spring i-Ready data and updating curriculum frameworks
Budget Amendment: Frank Adams presented the Tentative Amended FY26 Budget

The amendment was required to comply with Section 17-1.5 of the Illinois School Code, which limits administrative expenditure growth to 5% over the prior year; the original budget reflected a 6% increase
The original budget projected a $61,100 deficit; the amended budget reflects a $59,601 deficit, an improvement of about $1,500
Next steps: 30 days on public display, published hearing notice, a June budget hearing, and submission to ISBE and the Lake County Clerk
Action Items: Resolution to certify a proposition for a County School Facility Occupation Tax approved
